messages:
maya (support): FYI customer ACME reports a burst of 502s from our hosted API where they'd expect 429s. Ticket #12345. Example response attached.

liam (eng-sre): Can you paste the curl + response and any request_id?

maya (support): Curl: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'`
Response: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{\"error\":\"upstream error\",\"code\":500}`
Request-id: `rid-0abc123`

mike (oncall): I see a spike from 10:28:40 - 10:30:10 UTC where quota checks started timing out. Logs show quota-service returned a deadline error and proxy mapped it to 502. Suspect fallback mapping is wrong.

maya (support): Customer says it affects hosted inference endpoints across multiple regions, intermittent. They hit ~120 r/s for a minute and then ~40% responses 502.

liam (eng-sre): Paste of proxy log excerpt: ```
[2026-03-17T10:29:02Z] proxy: route=/v1/generate request_id=rid-0abc123 upstream=quota-service timeout=10s err=deadline exceeded
[2026-03-17T10:29:02Z] proxy: fallback=opaque_502 mapped_from=quota_timeout
```

jordan (infra): Deploy-bot shows a deploy at 2026-03-17T10:25:00Z for throttler-service (commit `a7c9f2e`). @deploy-bot can you confirm canary traffic?

deploy-bot: canary started at 10:25:00Z -> 10% traffic, auto-promote at 10:40:00Z (commit a7c9f2e). No rollbacks.

liam (eng-sre): That matches window. If throttler fallback mapping was changed in that release, it could propagate an internal dependency timeout to 502 instead of returning 429/slow-down. Jordan, can you check throttler config for fallback mappings and circuit breaker settings?

jordan (infra): Confirmed: new fallback handler introduced in `a7c9f2e` intended to surface detailed errors, but the mapping accidentally classifies quota timeouts as 5xx. Config snippet: ```
fallback_map: {dep_timeout: 502, dep_unavailable: 502}
```
Should be `dep_timeout -> 429`.

mike (oncall): Repro steps from customer: run `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}
' ...; done` at ~100r/s for 90s. We see ~40% 502. Attaching loop snippet.

maya (support): I've told the customer we're investigating and to expect updates. @ann make note for potential credit if SLA impacted.

ann (customer-success): Noted. Please flag if >5 min blip or any data loss. We may proactively offer credit.

liam (eng-sre): Jordan: hotfix plan? patch fallback_map and redeploy throttler. Also add monitoring to detect dep-timeout -> 5xx mapping.

jordan (infra): Pushing a hotfix to change mapping + add canary: ```
- dep_timeout: 502
+ dep_timeout: 429
```
Rolling 10% -> 100% now.

ratekeeper-bot: deploy triggered for throttler-service by jordan at 2026-03-17T10:52:00Z (patch b3f4d1). Canary 10% -> promoted to 100% at 10:56:00Z.

mike (oncall): Early canary metrics look good. Error spike for 502s drops to baseline, 429s increase slightly during throttling bursts (expected).

liam (eng-sre): Root cause quick summary: throttler fallback mapping introduced in recent deploy erroneously classified quota dependency timeouts as 5xx, causing proxy to return 502 instead of 429. Secondary cause: transient Redis/consensus latency in quota backend exacerbated the condition.

jordan (infra): Follow-ups: add circuit breaker + backoff in quota client, increase local cache TTL for token counts, add metric tag `fallback_origin=quota_dep_timeout` and alert on >1% rate of fallback->5xx.

maya (support): Customer updated: they confirm behavior now returns 429 during bursts instead of 502. They're still unhappy but appreciate fast fix.

ann (customer-success): Will coordinate credits if we see >1m of customer-facing 502. Please add postmortem link once available.

mike (oncall): Filing postmortem, assign to infra + eng-sre. Action items: revert risky fallback changes into gated feature flag until tested, add unit tests for fallback mappings, instrument more end-to-end checks for rate-limit flows.

liam (eng-sre): I'll own the postmortem. Adding tickets now.

maya (support): Closing loop with customer. Will update ticket #12345 and mark as resolved once CS confirms acceptance. :white_check_mark:
